scope: Reference reads and milestone closure: find_references with strict method search, reference kinds and target identity, and the prefix regression across all seven reads. Depends on CAP-READ-SYMBOLS and CAP-READ-TEXT-SEARCH. Wire JSON argument parsing, tool schemas, the LLM status/code/content envelope and rendering of read outcomes into ToolOutcome content are excluded and belong to the codec feature.

requirements.statement: find_references takes a symbol handle and a scope PROJECT (default) or LIBRARIES with the SR-005 meaning, except that references inside generated sources are included and marked generated. It returns every platform PsiReference in scope that resolves to the element, including import statements, Javadoc references ({@link}, @see) and references from non-Java files. A reference that resolves to a compiled library declaration is a reference to the equivalent declaration in its attached library source. Method search is strict: calls through a super method, calls to overriding methods and calls to overloads are not references to the handle's method. Every page carries the re-resolved target identity (kind, name, qualified owner, signature, declaration range and current document version, as in SR-008) and the scope used. Each reference has rendered path, a range of 0-based start and end-exclusive UTF-16 document offsets (the reference element start offset plus the reference range in that element), the 1-based line of the range start, a line excerpt (SR-010 excerpt rule with the range start as match start), a generated flag, a kind and the containing declaration (SR-025), absent when no catalog declaration encloses the reference. The kind is IMPORT for a reference inside a Java import statement, DOC for a reference inside a Java doc comment, and CODE otherwise. Unresolved text in comments or string literals and identifiers that resolve to a different element are not references. Results are ordered by rendered path, then start offset. Paged collection applies the result collection cap (SR-002): more results than the cap returns TOO_MANY_RESULTS with a narrowing hint and no page.

Semantic reads milestone closure. All seven read operations run through the frozen run driver in one IntelliJ fixture, and their outcomes, rendered by a test ModelItemRenderer and appended as accepted tool results through CacheGeneration, keep the prefix invariant (SR-022, product I13) across editor text changes, reindexing and file deletion between calls.

acceptance.when: Declare two unrelated classes with the same simple name in different packages, reference only one of them, then search_symbols and find_references for each.
acceptance.then: Both classes are separate candidates with different qualified owners; find_references for the referenced class returns exactly its references, and for the other class returns a complete page with no references.

acceptance.when: A class Base declares m(); Derived extends Base, overrides m() and declares an overload m(int). Code contains a call derived.m(), a call base.m() through a Base-typed variable, a call derived.m(1), a plain comment and a string literal containing 'm', a Javadoc {@link Derived#m()}, an unrelated class with its own m(), and a call to that unrelated m(). Separately, a class Util declares a static method u(); another file has a static import of Util.u, a generated source calls Util.u(), and a non-Java fixture file holds a platform-resolved reference to Util. Call find_references for the handles of Derived.m, Base.m, Util.u and Util.
acceptance.then: Derived.m returns exactly the derived.m() call with kind CODE and containing declaration, and the Javadoc link with kind DOC; the base.m() call, the derived.m(1) call, the plain comment, the string literal and the unrelated method's call are absent. Base.m returns exactly the base.m() call; derived.m() is absent. Util.u returns the static import with kind IMPORT and no containing declaration, and the generated call with kind CODE and the generated flag set. Util includes the non-Java reference with kind CODE. Every page carries the target's kind, name, qualified owner, signature, declaration range and document version, and the scope PROJECT; each reference range starts at the referenced name.

acceptance.when: With a test ModelItemRenderer, produce read outcomes, append them as accepted tool results through CacheGeneration, then change editor text, reindex and delete a file, and append further read outcomes.
acceptance.then: Every consecutive request extends the previous bytes exactly; no prefix violation occurs. This is a regression test; AC-023 proves SR-022 immutability.

acceptance.when: With the index wait bound injected as 200 ms, let a test reference query executor start dumb mode while find_references executes; in one case leave dumb mode after the bound, in another before it.
acceptance.then: The first returns INDEX_NOT_READY with no partial references; the second returns the complete reference list after the computation restarts.

acceptance.when: Hold smart mode constant. Request page one of find_references with limit 1, request page two without a change, repeat the page-two request with the same token, then make an unsaved document edit in the project and request page two again.
acceptance.then: Unchanged state continues in deterministic order to a complete final page, and the repeated request returns the same page again; the request after the unsaved edit returns STALE_PAGE.

acceptance.when: With the result collection cap injected as 3, call find_references for a symbol with 4 references.
acceptance.then: The call returns TOO_MANY_RESULTS with a narrowing hint and no page.

acceptance.when: Attach a library with a sources jar. Project code calls a method of a library class. Get the handles of that class and method with search_symbols in LIBRARIES scope, then call find_references with PROJECT scope on both handles.
acceptance.then: Both calls return the project reference that resolves to the compiled declaration.

acceptance.when: Make a test reference query executor throw an unexpected platform exception containing source text during find_references.
acceptance.then: The operation returns READ_FAILED with category INDEX_QUERY; the outcome and captured log contain no source text, argument or stack content.

type_safety_audit.invalid: A text occurrence reported as a reference, a reference to an unrelated same-name symbol, or a call through a super method reported for an overriding method
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: Reference entry construction is adapter-only (package-private) with a closed kind enum and a generated flag; every page carries target identity and scope components
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Adapter uses platform reference search for the resolved element with strict method search, computes ranges from the element offset plus the reference range, and classifies kind from the enclosing import statement or doc comment
type_safety_audit.justification: Reference resolution is live platform behavior

type_safety_audit.invalid: A milestone closure that proves each read in isolation but never appends read outcomes across changing IDE state
type_safety_audit.type_api_prevention: None beyond SR-022 immutable outcome values; the frozen CacheGeneration renders each accepted item once
type_safety_audit.residual_runtime_obligation: Prefix regression test (AC-019) over all seven operations
type_safety_audit.justification: Roadmap milestone 2 requires a prefix test across reads with changing editor and index state

assumptions: Requirement IDs are unique across the five semantic reads slices, which replace CAP-SEMANTIC-READS. A reference to a requirement outside this spec names the slice that owns it: read-domain SR-001, SR-002, SR-012, SR-014, SR-021, SR-022, SR-023, SR-024; read-pipeline SR-003, SR-004, SR-005, SR-015, SR-016, SR-019, SR-020, SR-026; read-text-search SR-010, SR-017; read-symbols SR-006, SR-007, SR-008, SR-011, SR-013, SR-018, SR-025; read-references SR-009, SR-027.

IntelliJ JUnit 5 test fixtures for a Java project with editors, libraries, generated and excluded roots, dumb mode and a test reference query executor are available through the IntelliJ Platform Gradle test framework configuration; the design may change plugin-core/build.gradle.kts for this and must keep tests discoverable as @Test methods.

Name and file indexes throw IndexNotReadyException in dumb mode (FileBasedIndexImpl). Reference search executors that are not dumb-aware block until smart mode when called without read access (QueryExecutorBase.java:57-66), so SR-016 requires calls inside the read computation. Dumb-mode entry runs a write action (DumbServiceImpl.kt:335-342), and a write action cancels a running non-blocking read computation, which reruns only when its constraints hold again (NonBlockingReadActionImpl.java:639-641,808-814). The platform exposes no partial-result signal for reference search; completeness is only complete or more results.

Normalizations of product terms: SR-025 range, signature, owner and containing-declaration definitions; SR-006 catalog declaration kinds; SR-003 line model and defaults; SR-004 path rendering and check order; SR-010 match and excerpt rule and skipped-file count; SR-020 READ_FAILED category rule; SR-026 failure precedence; SR-001 query validation; SR-004 canonical root comparison; SR-009 reference range, line and kind; SR-010 document offsets and match column; SR-025 parameter type text, array dimensions and compact constructors; SR-012 entry kinds.

Normalizations of scope: generated sources are omitted from find_file, unrestricted search_symbols and search_text directory scans, and included and marked in find_references so reference sets stay complete; handle reuse for the same element (SR-011) keeps one live handle per element in the registry.
The product rule 'reports partial search/index readiness separately' is satisfied by fail-closed INDEX_NOT_READY and TOO_MANY_RESULTS outcomes, because the platform gives no partial-result signal.

Java short-name stub lookups hide library source files unless library sources are included (JavaSourceFilterScope.java:36-51). A project reference to a compiled library class or method is equivalent to the declaration in its attached source (PsiClassImplUtil.java:1162-1228,1251-1273), so find_references on a library source handle finds project references.
